summary: Captures and blurs the camera's view once into a shared low-res texture every glass material samples.
overview: Drop it on the camera that renders the scene behind the UI. It captures and blurs that view into ONE shared, deliberately low-resolution RenderTexture published globally, so every glass-blur material samples the same texture with no per-element setup and no per-element cost.
useCases: Any glass effect where a per-element blur would be too expensive.

params.tuning: Low is the point — a quarter is usually indistinguishable once blurred, and costs a sixteenth of the pixels.
Repeated box blur cheaply approximates a Gaussian. Two or three passes is usually enough; more costs more for little visible gain.
The main cost control. A static pause menu can capture once and never again.

gotchas.title: One source for the whole scene
gotchas.body: It is a global texture, so every glass material shares it. Two cameras needing different blurred backdrops is not something this supports.

gotchas.title: It captures the camera's view, so UI drawn over it is not included
gotchas.body: Which is correct — otherwise the blur would feed back on itself.
